w08q1.intro: Three answers, always the same three: right, wrong, or it doesn't say. “It doesn't say” is the hard one, and in the test you chose it correctly. Trust that.

items.passage: Nina lives in a small house near the park with her mother and her brother. She walks to school every morning.
items.prompt: Nina has a sister.
items.teach: A brother is mentioned. A sister is neither confirmed nor denied — so it doesn't say. This is your item from the test.

items.passage: Nina lives in a small house near the park with her mother and her brother. She walks to school every morning.
items.prompt: Nina goes to school by bus.
items.teach: The text says she walks. That contradicts the bus, so it is wrong — not “doesn't say”.

items.passage: Nina lives in a small house near the park with her mother and her brother. She walks to school every morning.
items.prompt: Nina lives close to a park.

items.passage: Sam is nine. He plays football on Saturdays and he is learning the guitar. His favourite lesson at school is science.
items.prompt: Sam plays football at school.
items.teach: He plays on Saturdays; where, we are not told.

items.passage: Sam is nine. He plays football on Saturdays and he is learning the guitar. His favourite lesson at school is science.
items.prompt: Sam can already play the guitar very well.
items.teach: “Learning” tells you he is not finished. How good he is now is not stated.

items.passage: Sam is nine. He plays football on Saturdays and he is learning the guitar. His favourite lesson at school is science.
items.prompt: Sam likes science more than his other lessons.

w08q2.intro: Now the texts get longer — full A2 length, like KET Reading Part 4. The three answers are the same three.

items.passage: The city museum has a new room about the sea. You can touch a real shark's tooth and listen to whale songs through headphones. The museum is free for children, but adults pay four pounds. It opens at ten o'clock every day except Monday, when it stays closed all day.
items.prompt: Children can go into the museum without paying.

items.passage: The city museum has a new room about the sea. You can touch a real shark's tooth and listen to whale songs through headphones. The museum is free for children, but adults pay four pounds. It opens at ten o'clock every day except Monday, when it stays closed all day.
items.prompt: The museum is open on Mondays.
items.teach: “Except Monday” plus “stays closed all day” makes this wrong, not unknown.

items.passage: The city museum has a new room about the sea. You can touch a real shark's tooth and listen to whale songs through headphones. The museum is free for children, but adults pay four pounds. It opens at ten o'clock every day except Monday, when it stays closed all day.
items.prompt: There is a café inside the museum.

items.passage: Last summer my family went camping in the mountains. It rained on the first two days, so we stayed in the tent and played cards. On Wednesday the sun came out and we walked to a lake. My brother swam, but the water was far too cold for me.
items.prompt: It rained for the whole holiday.

items.passage: Last summer my family went camping in the mountains. It rained on the first two days, so we stayed in the tent and played cards. On Wednesday the sun came out and we walked to a lake. My brother swam, but the water was far too cold for me.
items.prompt: The writer swam in the lake.
items.teach: The brother swam. “Too cold for me” tells you the writer did not.

items.passage: Last summer my family went camping in the mountains. It rained on the first two days, so we stayed in the tent and played cards. On Wednesday the sun came out and we walked to a lake. My brother swam, but the water was far too cold for me.
items.prompt: The writer has one brother.
items.teach: “My brother” does not tell you he is the only one.

items.passage: Ben's grandmother teaches him to bake every Sunday afternoon. Last week they made bread for the first time. It took three hours and Ben got flour all over his jumper, but everyone said it was the best bread they had ever eaten.
items.prompt: Ben and his grandmother bake together every week.

items.passage: Ben's grandmother teaches him to bake every Sunday afternoon. Last week they made bread for the first time. It took three hours and Ben got flour all over his jumper, but everyone said it was the best bread they had ever eaten.
items.prompt: Ben has made bread many times before.

items.passage: Ben's grandmother teaches him to bake every Sunday afternoon. Last week they made bread for the first time. It took three hours and Ben got flour all over his jumper, but everyone said it was the best bread they had ever eaten.
items.prompt: Ben's jumper was new.

w08q3.intro: One more step: not just which answer, but which line of the text proved it.

items.passage: The swimming pool opens at seven in the morning. On Saturdays there is a lesson for beginners at nine, and the pool is very busy afterwards. Bring your own towel — the pool does not lend them.
items.prompt: “You must bring a towel.” Which line proves it?

items.passage: The swimming pool opens at seven in the morning. On Saturdays there is a lesson for beginners at nine, and the pool is very busy afterwards. Bring your own towel — the pool does not lend them.
items.prompt: The pool costs three pounds.

items.passage: Marta moved here from Poland two years ago. At first she found English very hard, especially the spelling, but now she reads a book in English every month. She still writes to her old friends in Polish.
items.prompt: Marta finds English spelling easy now.
items.teach: We know spelling was hard at first, and that she reads well now. Whether spelling itself got easier is never said.

items.passage: Marta moved here from Poland two years ago. At first she found English very hard, especially the spelling, but now she reads a book in English every month. She still writes to her old friends in Polish.
items.prompt: Marta writes to her friends in English.

items.passage: Marta moved here from Poland two years ago. At first she found English very hard, especially the spelling, but now she reads a book in English every month. She still writes to her old friends in Polish.
items.prompt: “Marta can read English well.” Which line proves it?
options: “she reads a book in English every month”
“moved here from Poland two years ago”
items.answer: “she reads a book in English every month”
